raw_affiliation_strings: Roger W. Sperry, Ph.D. Dr. Sperry is the Hixon Professor of Psychobiology at the California Institute of Technology. His research interests include psychobiology, neuropsychology, and neurobiology, with emphasis on: selective patterning in growth of nerve connections; neural mechanisms in perception and memory; split-brain approach to cerebral organization; mind-brain concepts and human value implications. He is a member of the National Academy of Sciences, the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, the American Philosophical Society, and the Royal Society. Among his many honors and awards are the California Scientist of the Year Award, the Wakeman Award of the National Paraplegic Foundation (1972), the Passano Award for Medical Research (1973), the Karl Lashley Award of the American Philosophical Society (1976), The Wolf Prize in Medicine (1979) and an Albert Lasker Basic Medical Research Award. He holds honorary doctorates from Cambridge University (1972) and the University of Chicago (1976) and The Rockefeller University (1980)
